passages.provision_quote: Following the implementation of the minimum wage increase specified in subparagraph (F) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), on or before August 1 of that year, and on or before each August 1 thereafter, the Director of Finance shall calculate an adjusted minimum wage. The calculation shall increase the minimum wage by the lesser of 3.5 percent and the rate of change in the averages of the most recent July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period over the preceding July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period for the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics nonseasonally adjusted United States Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (U.S. CPI-W). The result shall be rounded to the nearest ten cents ($0.10). Each adjusted minimum wage increase calculated under this subdivision shall take effect on the following January 1.
passages.note: The bill amends three Labor Code sections on one labor subject (wage floor plus IHSS sick days keyed to the wage thresholds), so it is not an omnibus; its operative wage section raises the floor on a schedule and then indexes it annually.

rows.reasoning: McGuire voted Aye on SB 3 (2015-2016), whose operative wage section raises the floor on a fixed schedule to fifteen dollars ($15) per hour and then directs that "the Director of Finance shall calculate an adjusted minimum wage" each year by the CPI-W formula, with each adjustment taking effect "on the following January 1". That is the rung that would "Raise the wage floor and tie it to the cost of living, so it rises automatically each year without new legislation", and the automatic indexing excludes the rung that would "adjust it only when lawmakers vote to".
